obligation: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act privacy and safeguards
basis: The bank, the broker-dealer and the investment adviser are financial institutions that hold nonpublic personal information of about 3.6 million consumer customers and 210,000 brokerage and advisory accounts. Safeguards duties are set by each entity's regulator: the OCC Guidelines for the bank (N52-R02) and Regulation S-P for the broker-dealer and adviser (N52-R05). Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards (OCC) with Supplement A; Federal Reserve version for the parent
citation: 12 CFR Part 30 Appendix B; 12 CFR Part 225 Appendix F
basis: Cris Santos Bank, N.A. is a national bank (App. B I.A); the parent is a bank holding company, covered by 12 CFR 225 App. F and met through the same enterprise program. No size exemption: the program must fit the bank's size and complexity (II.A). Primary regulation for these deliverables. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule
basis: The bank is OCC-supervised and the broker-dealer and adviser are SEC-regulated; no group entity is a financial institution under FTC jurisdiction for this rule. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation
basis: No group entity holds a license, registration or charter under the New York Banking, Insurance or Financial Services Law, and the bank has no New York branch or office. Rechecked at each new license, product or acquisition. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-P (2024 amendments)
applies: Yes, for the broker-dealer and adviser
basis: Cris Santos Investment Services, LLC is a registered broker-dealer and investment adviser, a covered institution (248.30(d)(3)); the larger-entity compliance date of 2025-12-03 has passed. Its 31 service providers with customer information include the clearing firm. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-ID (identity theft red flags)
applies: Yes, for the broker-dealer and adviser
basis: Registered broker-dealer and investment adviser that maintain covered accounts (248.201(a)); program approved 2024

obligation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668
citation: NAIC Model #668 as adopted by states
basis: The group has no insurance agency or underwriting subsidiary and holds no insurance license

obligation: SEC public-company cybersecurity disclosure
basis: The parent is an Exchange Act reporting company and a large accelerated filer, not a smaller reporting company; no exemption by size. The FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: NCUA security program and cyber incident notification
basis: No group entity is a credit union

obligation: OCC heightened standards for large banks (cited in the deliverables as App. D under N52-R02)
basis: Applies to a national bank with average total consolidated assets of $50 billion or more (App. D I.A; I.E.5). The regulatory reports show the parent's assets between $50 billion and $100 billion in each quarter and the bank's assets at more than 95% of the parent's, so the bank may use the parent's risk governance framework (I.3, I.4); independent risk management documented that assessment on 2026-01-19. The OCC proposal to raise the threshold (90 FR 61084, 2025-12-30) is not final. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Computer-security incident notification (bank)
basis: Applies to national banks (53.1(c)): notice to the OCC within 36 hours of determining a notification incident; bank service providers must notify the bank (53.4). The OCC point of contact is in the incident binder

obligation: Computer-security incident notification (parent)
basis: The parent is a U.S. bank holding company (225.300(c)); parallel 36-hour notice to the Federal Reserve. The Federal Reserve Bank's point of contact is in the incident binder

obligation: Federal Reserve risk committee rule (Regulation YY subpart C)
basis: A bank holding company with average total consolidated assets of $50 billion or more must keep a board risk committee and a chief risk officer; the parent's assets were below the $100 billion level where subpart D replaces subpart C. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: OCC identity theft red flags rule
basis: National bank that offers covered accounts (41.90(a)); written program with an annual report to the board risk committee

obligation: Suspicious activity reports (bank)
basis: National bank; cyber-enabled fraud cases are linked to BSA cases and SAR filings

obligation: Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B (credit models and adverse action)
basis: The bank is a creditor and uses models, including AI-001 and AI-002, in credit decisions; the CFPB supervises the bank for federal consumer financial law because its assets exceed $10 billion (12 U.S.C. 5515). Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FCRA adverse action notice
basis: The bank uses consumer reports from three consumer reporting agencies in underwriting

obligation: Regulation B subpart B (small business lending data)
basis: The bank expects to be a covered financial institution, but compliance is not yet required; the fair lending program tracks the compliance date. Rechecked in P03

obligation: Interagency revised model risk management guidance
basis: Guidance, not a rule; it says it is most relevant to banking organizations with more than $30 billion in total assets and excludes generative and agentic AI models from its scope. Applied in P10

obligation: State breach notification laws
citation: Statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Customers in Florida, Georgia, Alabama, South Carolina, North Carolina and Tennessee, and customers who live elsewhere; notify under the law of each state of residence using outside counsel's state matrix

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: The bank holds personal information of Florida residents and is headquartered in Florida. Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Funds transfers (refund of unauthorized payment orders; worked example)
citation: UCC Article 4A as enacted in the governing state (Florida: Fla. Stat. Chapter 670)
basis: Treasury management agreements set the governing law for commercial wire transfers; Florida is the worked example

obligation: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act
basis: Final rule not published at intake; counsel's memo lists it as an item to watch; reporting to CISA is voluntary until it takes effect. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: FDIC computer-security incident notification
basis: The OCC is the bank's primary federal regulator; Part 53 applies instead

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over financial reporting are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (issuer obligations)
basis: Card data is processed by the card processor; the bank's issuer obligations are handled in the card program

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom or extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; kept for extortion scenarios

obligation: Federal contract clauses on covered telecommunications and Kaspersky products
basis: No federal contracts in the contract repository; recheck if one is signed

obligation: Client agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (assurance reports, incident notice and availability terms)
basis: SL-1 clients receive an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report and SL-2 clients an annual SOC 1 Type 2 report; client agreements set service commitments and incident notice terms
